content.user_title: Map Skills to Clear Proficiency Levels
content.value_statement: Curricula often use subjective difficulty labels and omit prerequisites. This skill maps skills to CEFR, Bloom’s Taxonomy, and DigComp indicators for coherent learning progression.
actual_capabilities: Maps skills and lessons to CEFR, Bloom’s Taxonomy, and DigComp proficiency levels.
Defines measurable learner indicators for each proposed proficiency level.
Checks that skill sequences do not regress in proficiency.
Identifies missing prerequisites for dependent skills.
Suggests assessment types that match learner proficiency.
Applies five coherence checks for naming, progression, prerequisites, and connectivity.
limitations: It provides instructional guidance and does not certify learner proficiency.
It relies on the curriculum details and evidence supplied in the prompt.
It does not replace subject-matter experts or formal standards review.
Its CEFR mappings are adapted for general skills, not official language assessment.

use_cases.title: Sequence a technical course
use_cases.description: Map lessons in a programming course from foundational recognition to independent problem solving.

use_cases.title: Design assessment rubrics
use_cases.description: Create level-specific indicators and question types for a training program.

use_cases.title: Audit a learning pathway
use_cases.description: Find regression, missing prerequisites, and isolated skills across chapters.

prompt_templates.title: Map one skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the skill "writing user stories" to a CEFR level. Provide measurable indicators and one suitable assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a lesson sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A1 to B1 progression for SQL joins across four lessons. List prerequisites and measurable outcomes for each lesson.

prompt_templates.title: Review curriculum coherence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this course outline for proficiency regression, missing prerequisites, duplicate skill names, and isolated skills: [paste outline].

prompt_templates.title: Build a standards-aligned rubric
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CEFR and Bloom-aligned rubric for "debugging API integrations." Include B1 and B2 indicators, assessment tasks, and evidence requirements.

output_examples.input: Map "use spreadsheet formulas" for new analysts.
output: Indicator: The learner can enter and adapt basic SUM and IF formulas from a provided example.
Assessment: Complete a small budget sheet with three required formulas.

output_examples.input: Check this sequence: A1 variables, B1 functions, A2 debugging.
output: Issue: The sequence regresses from B1 to A2.
Recommendation: Place A2 debugging before B1 functions, or raise debugging outcomes to B1.

best_practices: Provide the learner audience, prior knowledge, time available, and target outcome.
Use observable actions and evidence instead of broad labels such as beginner or advanced.
Review full learning paths for prerequisites and non-decreasing proficiency.
anti_patterns: Assigning levels based only on intuition without measurable indicators.
Teaching dependent skills before their foundational prerequisites.
Using the same assessment task for every proficiency level.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses CEFR, Bloom’s Taxonomy, DigComp, and cognitive-load guidance described in the skill.

faq.question: Can it assess an individual learner?
faq.answer: It can suggest evidence and rubrics, but it does not provide formal certification or validated testing.

faq.question: Does CEFR apply only to languages?
faq.answer: The skill adapts CEFR-style progression descriptors to general learning skills.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide skills, lesson order, audience, prerequisites, available time, and desired outcomes.

faq.question: Can it find curriculum problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for regression, missing prerequisites, duplicate naming, and isolated skills.

faq.question: Can it create assessments?
faq.answer: It can recommend proficiency-matched assessment types and measurable rubric indicators.
